summary: Third of three Bodie Island towers: a banded 1872 brick lighthouse on the northern Outer Banks, still holding its first-order Fresnel lens, relit in 2013 after a four-year restoration.

notes_for_editor: Core history rests on the NRHP nomination (itself drawn from Holland 1967). Disagreements stated in the text: tower height (NRHP 164 ft; Outer Banks Voice 156 ft, which equals the Notice to Mariners focal plane), foundation of tower 3 (NRHP grillage vs LighthouseFriends pilings), and the 1872 assistants (LF Isaac Meekins/W. E. Etheridge vs USLHS Peter Johnston/W. E. Etheridge). The Bulletin item on the Swastika is in the 1915 volume; the year of April 22 is inferred from the volume. The 1900 report page was located by scan page (116); the printed page was not checked. The NRHP nomination's 1858-59 note says the second tower was razed in 1859; NPS and LF say it was abandoned. Record says tower 47 m; NRHP 164 ft = 50 m; recommend checking. Roster matched from the USLHS page, not checked against primary registers. Newspaper search (Chronicling America) found nothing usable. No keeper-name general period context was used. Lighthouse Friends says Rebecca was the only woman keeper at Bodie. Fact-check 2026-10-22: NRHP page numbers verified against page headers; LF narrative names Isaac Meekins as 1872 first assistant while LF's own roster agrees with USLHS (Peter Johnston).
